The wet–web strength of softwood\nﬁber had a more signiﬁcant increase when compared to that of hardwood ﬁber. It is for that ﬁber\nlength plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in\ncharacterizing the tensile strength of ﬁbers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that\nPFI reﬁning did not reduce ﬁber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24].\nThe above results showed that PFI reﬁning improved the extent of ﬁbrillation (especially the internal\nﬁbrillation), the swelling of ﬁbers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile\nstrength of ﬁbers.\n\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the ﬁber strength\nfor unreﬁned and reﬁned samples: (a) softwood ﬁbers and (b) hardwood ﬁbers.",
      "2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI reﬁner\n(Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency\nof 10%, the gap between the opposite reﬁning plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were\n3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus\n(Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "Table 1. (a) The CI of softwood ﬁbers through reﬁning. (b) The CI of hardwood ﬁbers through reﬁning.\n(a)\nCI (%) Crystallite Size (nm)\nRevolutions a b CI-XI CI-XA 110 (110) (200)\n0 73.23 40.46 3.2 3.5 4.5\n4000 70.42 37.71 3.1 3.4 4.6\n8000 72.54 39.65 3.2 3.4 4.6\n12,000 70.93 36.22 3.1 3.7 4.7\n16,000 69.82 34.20 3.2 3.5 4.7\n(b)\nCI (%) Crystallite Size (nm)\nRevolutions a b CI-XI CI-XA 110 (110) (200)\n0 75.55 47.16 3.1 3.1 4.5\n4000 73.01 36.26 3.1 3.3 4.7\n8000 75.06 42.35 3.1 3.5 4.8\n12,000 74.57 39.21 2.9 4.0 4.8\n16,000 73.55 38.01 3.0 3.7 4.7\na The CI-XI value was obtained from the ratio of the diﬀraction intensity. b The CI-XA value was obtained from the\nratio of the peak areas.\n\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers were all similar,\ndecreasing ﬁrst and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The ﬂuctuation of the\nCI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI reﬁning on the diﬀerent regions of cellulose.\nIn the ﬁrst reﬁning stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in\nthe crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting\non the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical\nand thermal action of PFI reﬁning. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of\ncrystalline region.\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microﬁbrils with 18\ncellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443,\nand 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28].\nThus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose\nIβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-ﬁbrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed\nside-by-side for both softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury",
      "Polymers 2020, 12, 2912 12 of 14\nThe results indicated that the ﬁbrillation and properties of ﬁbers are related to the variation of the\nsupramolecular structure during PFI reﬁning. It is noticeable that there was a signiﬁcantly positive\ncorrelation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI reﬁning for softwood\nﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally\nspeculated based on CI-XI while reﬁning. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of\nvarious H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI reﬁning is an excellent\nmechanical treatment of ﬁbrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\nSupplementary Materials: The following are available online at http://www.mdpi.com/2073-4360/12/12/2912/s1,\nFigure S1: XRD ﬁtting results of softwood ﬁbers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI\nreﬁning, Figure S2: XRD ﬁtting results of hardwood ﬁbers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions\nof PFI reﬁning, Figure S3: Nonlinear ﬁtting curves of the band of hardwood ﬁbers for hydroxyl groups: (a) 0, (b)\n4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI reﬁning, Figure S4: The BET N2 adsorption/desorption\nisotherms at various reﬁning revolutions of pulp ﬁbers: (a) softwood; (b) hardwood, Table S1: Cumulative pore\nvolume, average pore size and speciﬁc surface area of softwood pulp ﬁber through reﬁning, Cumulative pore\nvolume, average pore size and speciﬁc surface area of hardwood pulp ﬁber through reﬁning.\n\nAuthor Contributions: Conceptualization, methodology, software, validation, formal analysis, investigation,\ndata curation, writing—original draft preparation, and visualization: K.L.; conceptualization, validation, funding\nacquisition, writing—review and editing: L.Z.; conceptualization, resources, supervision, project administration,\nand funding acquisition: B.H. All authors have read and agreed to the published version of the manuscript.\nFunding: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (21706083), the Key\nArea R&D Program of Guangdong Province (2020B0101070001), and the National Key R&D Program of China\n(2017YFB0309501).\nConﬂicts of Interest: The authors declare no conﬂict of interest. The funders had no role in the design of the\nstudy; in the collection, analyses, or interpretation of data; in the writing of the manuscript, or in the decision to\npublish the results.\nReferences"
    ]
  }

MinerU85块＋全部既有优化 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内部纤丝化（使细胞壁分层、疏松和润胀）、外部纤丝化（从表面剥离仍附着的微纤丝）、纤维切断和细小纤维形成；这些作用提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [3]
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著升高；作者归因于更高纤丝化产生新表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
WRV升高表示的润胀使纤维横向更柔顺，从而有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
纸页抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI打浆过程中增加的纤丝化和细小纤维。 [2]
纤维长度对湿纸幅强度起重要作用；软木浆湿纸幅强度提高比硬木浆更显著。 [2]
软木纤维经PFI打浆后纤维长度呈下降趋势、细小纤维含量呈上升趋势；硬木纤维这些参数变化不如软木显著，可能与硬木所用打浆压力较低有关。 [1]
PFI打浆提高了内部纤丝化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，同时零-span抗张指数表明纤维本身强度未下降。 [2]
这些摘录未给出纤维长度、细小纤维、WRV对成纸强度的相对贡献或统计排序，因此无法判断三者中哪个贡献最大；缺少对三者的定量比较或归因分析。 [1] [2]

FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\nThe spectral was normalized $\\mathsf { a t 1 0 1 6 ~ c m ^ { - 1 } }$ and the derivative curve was obtained by applying the Savitzky–Golay algorithm. The wavenumbers of H-bonding components are taken from second-derivative spectra according to regions that are assigned to various H-bonds. Nonlinear fitting of the FT-IR spectral region from $\\bar { 3 } 0 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ to $3 7 0 0 ~ \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - \\mathrm { 1 } }$ was carried out with Gaussian function in Peakfit 4.12 software (SeaSolve Software Inc., Framingham, MA, USA). The Pearson correlation coeficients were evaluated between the CI and content of various H-bonds, with a statistically significant p-value of <0.05, while using Spss 25.0 statistics software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFor softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, the macro-fibrillation index and the fiber length had a downward trend, and the fines content has an upward trend for the softwood fibers during PFI refining, as can be seen in Figure 1. The macro-fibrillation index and fiber length of softwood fibers changed significantly. However, two parameters of hardwood fibers had no significant variations relative to softwood fibers. It might be because of the lower refining pressure that was applied in hardwood fibers. The macro-fibrillation index characterizes external macro-fibrillation. The results of fiber morphology analysis showed that external fibrillation increased with the refining process. It is consistent with the increasing specific surface area (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 1. The morphological analysis for the unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nThe beating degree and the WRV had a significant increment with increasing PFI refining revolutions, as can be seen in Figure 2. It is caused by the higher fibrillation that produces the new surface and more pores (as shown in Table S1 in Online Resource). The increase in swelling characterized by WRV makes the fibers more compliant in transverse [1], which contributes to improving the inter-fiber bonding strength of the fiber network. The results of fiber morphology analysis and water retention value showing that the fibrillation and the separation between fibrils increase with the refining process.",

The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.       "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that affects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coefficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n4.1.2 software). The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that there might be two microfibrils associated along part of their length.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nBecause the recorded infrared spectrum is the convolution of the real spectrum and the linear function of instrument. The band of hydroxyl groups $( 3 0 0 0 { - } 3 7 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ was deconvoluted into four predominant bands in the present study based on the peak positions above. Subsequently, the relative content of various H-bonds was calculated based on area proportion of the band, respectively. Finally, the data and curves obtained using nonlinear fitting for softwood fibers is shown in Table 2a and Figure 7, and the results of hardwood fibers can be seen in Table 2b and Figure S3.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds."

无法从这些摘录中确定针叶木打浆至8000转时的BET比表面积具体数值。 [1] [8]
摘录只说明，不同打浆转数下纤维的BET N2吸附/脱附等温线，以及针叶木浆纤维在各打浆转数下的累积孔体积、平均孔径和比表面积，都列在在线补充材料Table S1中；但这些摘录没有给出该表的数值。 [1]
现有摘录只指出，比表面积随打浆过程增大（见Table S1），未给出8000转对应的具体数值。 [8]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. MinerU85块＋全部既有优化 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

无法从这些摘录中列出针叶木8000转样品干纸抗张指数每次平行实验的原始数据。 [6]
摘录中涉及干纸抗张指数的内容只有图3的图题，说明其给出的是未精磨与精磨样品的抗张指数随精磨转数变化的曲线，并未列出8000转的具体数值。 [6]
干纸抗张强度按TAPPI T494测试，但摘录未给出该组的平行样数量、各次测量值或均值与标准差。 [4]
摘录中针叶木8000转的数值只有结晶指数（CI-XI 72.54%、CI-XA 39.65%）与晶粒尺寸，并非抗张指数数据。 [1]
表2a中针叶木8000转的数值为氢键相对含量（如O(6)H···O(3′)为28.43%），同样不是抗张指数数据。 [2]
所列补充材料包括XRD拟合图、羟基非线性拟合曲线、BET等温线及孔径/比表面积表，其中未见抗张指数平行实验原始数据表。 [3]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nSupplementary Materials: The following are available online at http://www.mdpi.com/2073-4360/12/12/2912/s1, Figure S1: XRD fitting results of softwood fibers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S2: XRD fitting results of hardwood fibers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S3: Nonlinear fitting curves of the band of hardwood fibers for hydroxyl groups: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S4: The BET N2 adsorption/desorption isotherms at various refining revolutions of pulp fibers: (a) softwood; (b) hardwood, Table S1: Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of softwood pulp fiber through refining, Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of hardwood pulp fiber through refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4.       "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the fiber strength for unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nSupplementary Materials: The following are available online at http://www.mdpi.com/2073-4360/12/12/2912/s1, Figure S1: XRD fitting results of softwood fibers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S2: XRD fitting results of hardwood fibers: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S3: Nonlinear fitting curves of the band of hardwood fibers for hydroxyl groups: (a) 0, (b) 4000, (c) 8000, (d) 12,000, (e) 16,000 revolutions of PFI refining, Figure S4: The BET N2 adsorption/desorption isotherms at various refining revolutions of pulp fibers: (a) softwood; (b) hardwood, Table S1: Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of softwood pulp fiber through refining, Cumulative pore volume, average pore size and specific surface area of hardwood pulp fiber through refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. The funders had no role in the design of the study; in the collection, analyses, or interpretation of data; in the writing of the manuscript, or in the decision to publish the results.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFigure 7. The deconvoluted FT-IR spectra of softwood fibers at various revolutions: (a) 0 r, (b) 4000 r, (c) 8000 r, (d) 12,000 r, and (e) 16,000 r.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the fiber strength for unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25].",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n4.1.2 software). The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that there might be two microfibrils associated along part of their length.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. The band of hydroxyl groups $( 3 0 0 0 { - } 3 7 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ was deconvoluted into four predominant bands in the present study based on the peak positions above. Subsequently, the relative content of various H-bonds was calculated based on area proportion of the band, respectively. Finally, the data and curves obtained using nonlinear fitting for softwood fibers is shown in Table 2a and Figure 7, and the results of hardwood fibers can be seen in Table 2b and Figure S3.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds."

PyMuPDF结构81块基线 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

PFI精磨提高了干纸的抗张强度，主要归因于精磨过程中细纤维化（尤其内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和细组分的增加。 [1]
零-span抗张指数结果表明PFI精磨没有降低纤维本身的抗张强度，因此干纸抗张性能的提高并非来自单根纤维强度下降。 [1]
所给证据涉及的力学测试与结果包括干纸抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零-span抗张强度，未提供同一批样品的耐破指数和撕裂指数精确数据。 [1] [4]

MinerU85块＋全部既有优化 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

PFI精磨提高了纤维细纤维化程度（尤其是内部细纤维化）、纤维润胀和干纸抗张强度，且未降低纤维本身的抗张强度。 [2]
干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI精磨过程中细纤维化和细组分的增加。 [2]
零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI精磨没有降低纤维强度。 [2]
所提供的摘录未包含耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数值，因此无法给出同批样品的这两项数据；缺少原文中对应的结果表、图或补充数据。 [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that affects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coefficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1).       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 2. The beating degree and Water Retention Value (WRV) for the unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.1. The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nFigure 3. The rheological analysis of wet sheets, the tensile strength of dry sheets, and the fiber strength for unrefined and refined samples: (a) softwood fibers and (b) hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds."

PyMuPDF结构81块基线 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

所给证据仅涉及Li等2020年关于PFI精磨对纤维素聚集结构影响的论文，未包含《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》的实验数据，故无法完成两篇论文全部实验数据的比较。 [4]
由于缺少另一篇论文的数据，无法基于所给证据给出两篇论文的共同结论。 [4]
PFI精磨过程中，纤维素的晶型、氢键距离以及各氢键的能量基本保持不变，而结晶指数、微晶尺寸和各氢键含量随精磨发生变化。 [4]
分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键的含量与由XRD峰强度得到的结晶指数显著正相关，Pearson相关系数在软木纤维中为0.888、在硬木纤维中为0.889（p<0.05）。 [4]
该研究认为PFI精磨是一种对超分子结构破坏相对较小的优良机械纤丝化处理。 [1]

Introduction\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired\nphysical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic ﬁbers. Therein,\nPapirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) reﬁning is the most common laboratory reﬁner in order to\nimprove the inter-ﬁber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-ﬁbrillated\nor nano-ﬁbrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on ﬁbers are: (i) internal\nﬁbrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of ﬁber wall; (ii) external ﬁbrillation—peeling of\nﬁbrils from the ﬁber surface while remaining attached; (iii) ﬁber shortening—ﬁber cutting due to\nshearing action, and (iv) ﬁnes formation—primary ﬁnes come from ray cells and parenchyma cells\nand microﬁbrils that are caused by ﬁber shortening or external ﬁbrillation. Moreover, the PFI reﬁning\ncould be adopted to obtain a higher internal ﬁbrillation than other laboratory reﬁners [1]. These eﬀects\nof the PFI reﬁning on cellulosic ﬁbers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the ﬂexibility, and the\ninter-ﬁber bonding capacity of ﬁbers. It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and\nproperties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during reﬁning [7,8].\n\nThere are some diﬀerent conclusions regarding to the eﬀects of PFI reﬁning on crystallinity of\ncellulose, not like that of ball milling, which eﬀectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment\nprogresses. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially\nﬂuctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating ﬂuctuation with PFI reﬁning for\ntobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identiﬁed a clear trend, but the results\nwere that the crystallinity varied during PFI reﬁnement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in\ncrystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during\nPFI reﬁning.\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure,\ncan be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl\ngroups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding\ndistance during deligniﬁcation [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used\nto study the diﬀerences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal\nregion [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during\nPFI reﬁning, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of\neucalyptus ﬁbers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that\nthe H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions\nof the content of certain H-bonds diﬀered at various reﬁning stages.\n\nThere is still a lack of literature on the eﬀects of PFI reﬁnement on the H-bonding network.\nParticularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of\nfurther study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of\nH-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, ﬂexibility,\nand ﬁbrillation of cellulosic ﬁbers during PFI reﬁnement. Therefore, this work explored the eﬀects\nof PFI reﬁnement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of\nH-bonds for softwood pulp ﬁbers and hardwood pulp ﬁbers. Attempts were made in order to establish\nthe correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n2. Methods\n\n2.1. PFI Reﬁning\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp ﬁbers were obtained from\nZhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI reﬁner\n(Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency\nof 10%, the gap between the opposite reﬁning plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were\n3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood ﬁbers and hardwood ﬁbers, respectively. The drainability was\ncharacterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp\nﬁbers were separately reﬁned in a PFI reﬁner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and\nat 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an\nincreasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79◦SR, were obtained for softwood ﬁbers and 0,\n26, 40, 57, and 70◦SR were obtained for hardwood ﬁbers.\n\n2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\nThe ﬁnes content, weighted mean length, and macro-ﬁbrillation index of each sample were\ndetermined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of\ndry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT\n12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus\n(Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

      "polymers\nArticle\nProbing Eﬀect of Papirindustriens Forskningsinstitut\n(PFI) Reﬁning on Aggregation Structure of Cellulose:\nCrystal Packing and Hydrogen-Bonding Network\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao * and Beihai He\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd.,\nTianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.)\n* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that aﬀects the properties of cellulosic\nﬁbers. MinerU85块＋全部既有优化 · 要点 2/2；边界 2/2

提供的证据仅包含Li-2020 PFI论文的摘录，未包含《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》的实验数据或结论，因此无法对两篇论文的全部实验数据进行逐项比较，也无法据此给出两篇的共同结论。 [1] [2]
PFI论文结论认为，PFI refining过程中纤维的纤维化及性能与超分子结构变化相关。 [2]
该文报告软木纤维和硬木纤维中CI-XI与O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量在PFI refining过程中呈显著正相关。 [2]
该文结论称晶粒尺寸、结晶度和各种氢键含量总体变化不大，并推测PFI refining是对超分子结构破坏相对较小的机械纤维化处理。 [2]
该文实验结论还称PFI refining提高了纤维化程度（尤其内部纤维化）、纤维溶胀和纸张抗张强度，且未降低纤维本身的抗张强度。 [6]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.",

Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4.       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets\n[原文]\nThe fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.",

The Morphological Analysis, Swelling, and Mechanical Properties\n[原文]\nIn Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.       "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.4. Correlation between CI and Content of Inter-Molecular H-Bonds during PFI Refining\n[原文]\nThe correlation between the CI-XI and the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH(2) and OH(6) was poor for the following reasons. The free OH groups are easier for forming the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds as opposed to the O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds in the amorphous region, because the distance between adjacent glucose units in a cellulosic molecular chain is closer than between the glucose units in the adjacent molecular chain (as shown in Figure 9). Accordingly, when compared with the content of O(6)H· · · O(3′) H-bonds, there was less difference in the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds or the free OH groups between the crystalline region and amorphous region, which sometimes made the content of the two bonds not change much in regards to the crystallinity. The O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds is stable, as mentioned above. It was presumed to change little as crystallinity changed during PFI refining. Hence, the correlation between O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds and the CI-XI was not discussed in the present study.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nupramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nBecause the recorded infrared spectrum is the convolution of the real spectrum and the linear function of instrument. The band of hydroxyl groups $( 3 0 0 0 { - } 3 7 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$ was deconvoluted into four predominant bands in the present study based on the peak positions above. Subsequently, the relative content of various H-bonds was calculated based on area proportion of the band, respectively. Finally, the data and curves obtained using nonlinear fitting for softwood fibers is shown in Table 2a and Figure 7, and the results of hardwood fibers can be seen in Table 2b and Figure S3.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b). On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H···O(3′) H-bonds.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n4.1.2 software). The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that there might be two microfibrils associated along part of their length.",
      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Effect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show. In general, the CI-XI and the CI-XA of softwood fibers showed a reduction of 4.66% and 15.47%, respectively, and those of hardwood fibers decreased by 2.65% and 19.4%, respectively, as can be seen in Figure 4 and Table 1. The value of the CI-XI was remarkably higher than the CI-XA, which might be caused by the over-fitting of amorphous contribution in the analysis of CI-XA. However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated significantly for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, with a correlation coefficient of 0.919 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.925 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25]."
    ]
  }
}
